subject: RFI: Abuse Detection, Triage & Escalation Playbook — SafeBank
messages:

Subject: Request: abuse detection playbook and evidence artifacts

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this. SafeBank's InfoSec team needs a granular view of Redwood's operational controls around content abuse/misuse detection for our vendor risk assessment. Specifically we're asking for:

- A playbook that describes detection signals, scoring, and automated mitigations (rate limits, throttling, model fallback).
- The triage and human-review workflow: routing, SLAs, severity levels, and escalation contacts.
- What evidence artifacts you can provide for audits (redacted logs, incident manifests, sample detection logs).
- Configurability for customers: per-customer policy toggles, webhook/reporting options, and retention/deletion controls.
- Any certifications or attestations you lean on (SOC 2, penetration testing summaries).

Can you deliver a single consolidated PDF plus a sample CSV of anonymized incident logs by EOD next Wednesday (2026-02-18)? Also flag any items that would require an NDA or additional legal review.

Appreciate it — let me know if you want to schedule a 30-min review call.

Best,
Aisha Qureshi
Head of Platform Security
SafeBank

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. We're able to produce the consolidated playbook and a pared-down anonymized CSV containing schema-aligned incident rows. Delivery plan: 

- Draft playbook (PDF) with detection, triage, escalation, and evidence list — by Mon 2026-02-16 (internal draft)
- Finalized playbook + sample CSV + evidence manifest — by Wed 2026-02-18 EOD

High-level notes up front:
- Detection: combination of model-surface classifiers, heuristic rules (rate/behavioral), and downstream anomaly scoring. We surface a continuous risk score (0-100) per request and bucket incidents into severity tiers (P1–P4).
- Triage: automatic routing to human-review queue for incidents above configurable thresholds; we provide human reviewer audit trails and annotation fields.
- Escalation: built-in webhook to customer SOC, optional email escalation, and Redwood on-call for P1 outages/abuse investigations.
- Evidence: we will include redacted request/response context (token hashes, timestamps), internal detector signals, and a manifest describing redaction heuristics.
- Compliance: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; we also provide ephemeral access logs for evidence requests.

Attached for initial reference: redwood_abuse_detection_playbook.pdf (overview) — it's illustrative; the final will include the CSV sample and manifest.

If you want to lock a 30-min sync, I'm available Mon afternoon PT.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

Karthik / Mina / Neha,

Quick internal checklist for the SafeBank packet — please make sure the final playbook explicitly calls out the following items (they're likely to ask during procurement):

1) Severity & SLA table: what constitutes P1/P2/P3/P4; acknowledgement and initial triage SLAs (we should propose: ack within 4 hours for P1, 24 hours for P2).
2) Customer-controlled mitigations: per-customer policy toggles (blocklist, rate caps, model-variant fallback) and how to apply them via API/console.
3) Evidence package contents and retention: default retention policy, on-demand exports, anonymization approach (token hashing + noise to preserve privacy).
4) Auditability: immutable audit logs, signed manifests for exported evidence, and a sample schema for misuse_incident_log_sample.csv.
5) False positive handling: appeal workflow, human-review SLA, and how we roll back automated mitigations.
6) Data residency/segregation: note our Dedicated/Private deployment options for regulated customers.

Mina — can you add a short paragraph on our detector architecture (ensemble model + rule engine + rate heuristics) and any limitations (e.g., detection lag at extreme low-signal scenarios)? Neha — pull the current SOC 2 summary link and note the scope (if redaction needed, flag).

I want the playbook to be concrete but not include raw customer data — use sanitized examples. Karthik, once you have the final, I can help run it by Legal for any extra redaction or NDA notes.

-Rishi
Director, Revenue — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Request: abuse detection playbook and evidence artifacts — final package

Hi Aisha — attaching the finalized materials per your RFI request. Summary below and highlights we call out in the playbook. Please see attachments and the Drive link for larger artifacts.

Attachments included in this message: redwood_abuse_detection_playbook.pdf (final), misuse_incident_log_sample.csv (anonymized), evidence_package_manifest.txt

Highlights (excerpt):

1) Detection & scoring
- Signals: model classifier outputs (probabilities), request heuristics (rate, requester fingerprinting), post-generation checks (toxicity/illicit content heuristics), and anomaly detectors.
- Score: normalized 0–100 risk score; thresholding is configurable per customer. We aim for operational detection precision > 92% on high-confidence bins and tune thresholds by workload.

2) Triage & human review
- Automatic routing: incidents where score >= configurable threshold are routed to human review queues with contextual metadata.
- Review metadata: reviewer id, timestamps, decision (block/allow/modify), notes. We retain reviewer audit trails for the configured retention window.

3) Escalation & timelines
- Severity mapping: P1 (confirmed active exploitation), P2 (high-confidence policy violation), P3 (possible misuse, manual review), P4 (informational).
- SLAs: initial acknowledgement — P1: 4 hours, P2: 24 hours. Investigation ETA: P1: 72 hours, P2: 5 business days. For Dedicated/Private customers, tighter SLAs are available via SOW.

4) Evidence package contents
- For each incident export: anonymized request id (hashed), timestamps, truncated request/response context (where required), detector signals, and internal decision logs. See misuse_incident_log_sample.csv for schema (columns: event_id, event_ts, risk_score, detector_flags, action_taken, reviewer_id_hash).
- Manifest file (evidence_package_manifest.txt) enumerates included files, redaction steps, and signer metadata for audit.

5) Customer integrations & reporting
- Webhooks: real-time incident webhook with configurable payload; delivery retry/backoff policy documented. Typical webhook latency SLO: < 2s for successful delivery.
- Console & API: incident search, exports, and per-customer policy toggles (blocklists, rate caps, model-variant selection).

6) Data retention & redaction
- Default retention: 90 days for incident artifacts; adjustable per contract (30–365 days supported).
- Redaction: token hashing + deterministic truncation; we never include raw PII in exports unless explicitly requested under an executed data-sharing Addendum.

7) False positive handling & appeals
- Appeal flow: customer requests review via support portal -> human re-evaluation -> decision within 3 business days (expedited for P1/P2). Automated mitigations can be rolled back via API by the customer or by Redwood on behalf of the customer with explicit audit.

8) Compliance & auditability
- Redwood holds SOC 2 Type II (scope summary in linked doc). We provide signed manifests for evidence exports and a time-ordered audit trail for each incident. For higher assurance customers, we offer Dedicated/Private deployments and support for on-site audits.

Next steps & deliverables: full packet uploaded to Drive (link below), a DocuSign envelope for an evidence-sharing Addendum if SafeBank requires expanded access, and an offer to run a 60-min technical walkthrough with our IR lead.

Regards,

Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
